observation.answer:
**Most relevant precedent clause (Candidate Clause 001)**  

> *Subject to requirements of applicable law, FCE will provide notice to ExxonMobil prior to, or promptly after, it becomes aware of any such **Change in Control**, and if prior notice is prohibited by applicable Law, as soon as practicable or after such notice is no longer prohibited, but in no event later than one (1) business day after any public announcement with respect to any such asset transfer or **Change in Control**.  
> 
>  ExxonMobil may terminate this Agreement upon fifteen (15) days written notice, without penalty, payment or prejudice to claims and obligations then accrued, if FCE undergoes a **Change in Control**.*  

**Citation:** ACORD Clause Bank – Change Of Control (document ID `6a2aacc8df796b0bc54e4515`), *Candidate Clause 001*, page 1.  

**Why this clause is the best match:**  
- Directly defines the parties’ obligations when a **Change of Control** occurs (notice requirement).  
- Includes the termination right triggered by a **Change of Control**, which is a core element attorneys typically seek.  
- All other candidate clauses in the document address unrelated topics (e.g., term length) and are therefore less relevant.

The clause appears on **page 1** of the document and reads:

> “Subject to requirements of applicable law, **FCE will provide notice to ExxonMobil prior to, or promptly after, it becomes aware of any such Change in Control**, and if prior notice is prohibited by applicable Law, as soon as practicable or after such notice is no longer prohibited, but in no event later than one (1) business day after any public announcement with respect to any such asset transfer or **Change in Control**.  
> 
> **ExxonMobil may terminate this Agreement upon fifteen (15) days written notice, without penalty, payment or prejudice to claims and obligations then accrued, if FCE undergoes a Change in Control**.  
> 
> Notwithstanding anything else in this Agreement, in the event of termination under this Paragraph 12.04 ExxonMobil may terminate any licenses granted to FCE under this Agreement that would otherwise survive termination, taking into account the circumstances surrounding the Change in Control.”

**Answer to the attorney’s query (“Change of Control”)**  

The single most relevant precedent clause is the one quoted above (Candidate Clause 001). It directly defines the parties’ obligations when a Change of Control occurs, specifies the required notice procedure, and provides the termination right that may be exercised by the counter‑party upon such an event. This clause should be used as the primary reference for drafting or negotiating Change of Control provisions.

**Best‑matching precedent clause (Candidate Clause 001)**  

> *Subject to requirements of applicable law, **FCE will provide notice to ExxonMobil prior to, or promptly after, it becomes aware of any such Change in Control**, and if prior notice is prohibited by applicable Law, as soon as practicable or after such notice is no longer prohibited, **but in no event later than one (1) business day after any public announcement** with respect to any such asset transfer or Change in Control.  
> 
> **ExxonMobil may terminate this Agreement upon fifteen (15) days written notice**, without penalty, payment or prejudice to claims and obligations then accrued, if FCE undergoes a Change in Control.*  

**Citation:** ACORD Clause Bank – Change Of Control, *Candidate Clause 001*, page 1, Document ID `6a2aacc8df796b0bc54e4515` (excerpt shown in the document header).  

### Calculated values from the clause  

| Item | Value stated in the clause | Interpretation / calculation |
|------|----------------------------|------------------------------|
| **Notice deadline after a public announcement** | “one (1) business day” | The obligor must give notice **no later than 1 business day** after the public announcement of a Change in Control. |
| **Termination notice period** | “fifteen (15) days written notice” | The counter‑party may terminate the agreement by delivering **15 calendar days** written notice once a Change in Control occurs. |

No monetary caps, percentages, or other quantitative limits are present in this clause; the only quantitative provisions are the two time‑based deadlines shown above.  

**Answer to the attorney’s query:**  
The clause above is the most directly relevant precedent for a Change of Control provision. It sets a **1‑business‑day notice deadline** for the party undergoing the change and grants the other party a **15‑day written‑notice termination right** upon such an event. These are the only calculable parameters in the clause.

**Best‑matching precedent clause (Candidate Clause 001)**  

> *Subject to requirements of applicable law, **FCE will provide notice to ExxonMobil prior to, or promptly after, it becomes aware of any such Change in Control**, and if prior notice is prohibited by applicable Law, as soon as practicable or after such notice is no longer prohibited, **but in no event later than one (1) business day after any public announcement** with respect to any such asset transfer or Change in Control.  
> 
> **ExxonMobil may terminate this Agreement upon fifteen (15) days written notice**, without penalty, payment or prejudice to claims and obligations then accrued, if FCE undergoes a Change in Control.*  

**Citation:** ACORD Clause Bank – Change Of Control, *Candidate Clause 001*, page 1, Document ID `6a2aacc8df796b0bc54e4515` (excerpt shown in the document header).  

### Calculated values from the clause  

| Item | Value stated in the clause | Interpretation / calculation |
|------|----------------------------|------------------------------|
| **Notice deadline after a public announcement** | “one (1) business day” | The obligor must give notice **no later than 1 business day** after the public announcement of a Change in Control. |
| **Termination notice period** | “fifteen (15) days written notice” | The counter‑party may terminate the agreement by delivering **15 calendar days** written notice once a Change in Control occurs. |

No monetary caps, percentages, or other quantitative limits are present in this clause; the only quantitative provisions are the two time‑based deadlines shown above.  

**Answer to the attorney’s query:**  
The clause above is the most directly relevant precedent for a Change of Control provision. It sets a **1‑business‑day notice deadline** for the party undergoing the change and grants the other party a **15‑day written‑notice termination right** upon such an event. These are the only calculable parameters in the clause.

**Recommended precedent clause (most directly addresses multiple possible governing laws)**  

> “This Agreement will be governed by the laws of the state where a suit is properly filed.”【6a2aadb1df796b0bc54e451e:macro_0_295e8cc048】

**Explanation**  
- The clause does not fix a single jurisdiction; instead it ties the governing law to the state in which any litigation is commenced. This provides for *multiple* potential governing laws, satisfying the request for a “clause with multiple governing laws.”  
- No numerical calculations (cap, period, percentage, deadline) are required or present in this clause.  

*All other candidate clauses in the document (e.g., Texas‑only, English‑only, New York‑only) specify a single governing law and are therefore less relevant to the query.*

**Why this clause is the best match**

- It explicitly addresses **transferred or licensed intellectual property**, which is the core of an IP ownership assignment or transfer query.  
- It includes the key warranties/representations that the IP will be free from infringement and that neither party is required to file or maintain patents—typical provisions in IP‑assignment clauses.  
- The clause is tagged with **assignment**, **obligation**, and **warranty**, confirming its relevance.  

*Confidence:* **high** – the clause directly discusses the transfer of IP rights and related obligations.

**Most relevant precedent clause for “IP Ownership Assignment or Transfer”**

> “Parties or the use of any **Transferred IP** or **Licensed IP** will be free from infringement of any Intellectual Property; or (v) imposing on either party any obligation to file any patent application or to secure any patent or maintain any patent.”  
> — *Document Preamble → Fitness For Any Particular Purpose, Or Title Or Non‑Infringement / Section 3.11 No Other Warranties or Covenants*【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:meso_92221_7dbc576f05】

**Calculation of any numeric term**  
The clause contains no explicit numbers (e.g., caps, periods, percentages, or deadlines). Therefore, no calculation is applicable.  

**Result** – The above clause is the single most pertinent precedent for an IP‑ownership assignment or transfer in the ACORD clause‑bank. It affirms that transferred or licensed IP must be non‑infringing and that neither party is required to file or maintain patents. No numeric values are present to compute.

spans.text: In addition, IAC shall secure any and all Intellectual Property Rights that may pertain to the Sonos Products that are created by such IAC Subcontractor, and hereby transfers and assigns all such Intellectual Property Rights<omitted>Any Product Customizations made by IAC or an IAC Subcontractor shall be on a "work for hire" (using the meaning given to such term under United States copyright law) basis to the maximum extent permissible under applicable law, and all Intellectual Property Rights therein shall be owned solely by Sonos.<omitted>IAC shall cooperate fully with Sonos and execute such further instruments, documents and agreements and give such further written assurances, as may be reasonably requested by Sonos, at Sonos' expense, to perfect the foregoing assignment and obtain and enforce assigned Intellectual Property Rights.<omitted>Except for preexisting IAC Property and any third party's Intellectual Property, IAC shall and does hereby irrevocably assign, and shall and does cause IAC Affiliates and IAC Subcontractors to irrevocably assign, to Sonos all of IAC's, IAC Affiliates' or IAC Subcontractors' worldwide right title and interest in and to the Sonos Property , if any, whether developed solely by Sonos or jointly between Sonos or a Sonos Affiliate and IAC, an IAC Affiliate, or an IAC Subcontractor, that<omitted>may arise through the performance of its obligations under this Agreement.

observation.answer:
Below is a **proposed tabular review** of the most relevant precedent candidates for the attorney’s “IP Ownership Assignment or Transfer” query.  The table includes a ranking, a short excerpt of each candidate clause, a brief relevance rationale, suggested drafting use, and the citation to the evidence record.  

| Rank | Candidate Clause (excerpt) | Relevance Rationale | Drafting Use (suggested way to incorporate) | Citation |
|------|----------------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------------|----------|
| 1 | “Parties or the use of any **Transferred IP** or **Licensed IP** will be free from infringement of any Intellectual Property; or (v) imposing on either party any obligation to file any patent application or to secure any patent or maintain any patent.” | Directly addresses the core concepts of **IP transfer/assignment** and the warranties that the transferred IP is non‑infringing and that no further patent‑filing obligations are imposed. | Insert as a **representation and warranty** clause in the IP‑assignment section of the agreement, or as a stand‑alone “IP Ownership” clause. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:meso_92221_7dbc576f05】 |
| 2 | “From and against any and all liabilities, obligations, losses, damages, taxes, claims, actions and suits, and any and all reasonable out‑of‑pocket costs, expenses and disbursements (including reasonable legal fees …).” (Clause 9.15 – Disclaimer of Special Damages) | Contains the tag **assignment** and a broad disclaimer of liability that could be useful when limiting exposure after an IP transfer. | Use as a **limitation‑of‑liability** add‑on to the IP‑assignment clause, especially if the parties wish to cap post‑transfer claims. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_72087_3deb75ce46】 |
| 3 | “Janssen shall indemnify and hold harmless Company, its Affiliates and its and their …” (Clause 12.1.1 – Indemnification) | While not an IP‑assignment clause per se, it provides a **general indemnification** framework that can be tailored to cover IP‑related breaches. | Adapt the indemnity language to create an **IP‑infringement indemnification** provision accompanying the assignment. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_33409_c92ab54a6c】 |
| 4 | “Within thirty (30) days after delivery of such notification, the Indemnifying Party may …” (Clause 12.2.2 – Notice deadline) | Includes a **deadline** and the tag **assignment**, useful for setting a response period for IP‑related notices (e.g., notice of infringement). | Add a **notice‑and‑cure** timeline for IP‑ownership disputes after transfer. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_46790_48db6dbb7a】 |
| 5 | “The Party not controlling such defense shall reasonably cooperate with the other Party.” (Clause 12.2.3 – Cooperation) | Provides a **cooperation** obligation that can be applied to joint defense of IP infringement claims after assignment. | Insert as a **co‑defense cooperation** clause in the IP‑assignment section. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_47668_1a305a53e5】 |

**Next step:** Please review the proposed table. If it looks good, I can create the formal tabular review artifact (e.g., a structured review in ContractSense) for you. Let me know if you’d like any changes or to proceed.

Below is a **proposed tabular review** of the most relevant precedent candidates for the attorney’s “IP Ownership Assignment or Transfer” query.  The table includes a ranking, a short excerpt of each candidate clause, a brief relevance rationale, suggested drafting use, and the citation to the evidence record.  

| Rank | Candidate Clause (excerpt) | Relevance Rationale | Drafting Use (suggested way to incorporate) | Citation |
|------|----------------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------------|----------|
| 1 | “Parties or the use of any **Transferred IP** or **Licensed IP** will be free from infringement of any Intellectual Property; or (v) imposing on either party any obligation to file any patent application or to secure any patent or maintain any patent.” | Directly addresses the core concepts of **IP transfer/assignment** and the warranties that the transferred IP is non‑infringing and that no further patent‑filing obligations are imposed. | Insert as a **representation and warranty** clause in the IP‑assignment section of the agreement, or as a stand‑alone “IP Ownership” clause. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:meso_92221_7dbc576f05】 |
| 2 | “From and against any and all liabilities, obligations, losses, damages, taxes, claims, actions and suits, and any and all reasonable out‑of‑pocket costs, expenses and disbursements (including reasonable legal fees …).” (Clause 9.15 – Disclaimer of Special Damages) | Contains the tag **assignment** and a broad disclaimer of liability that could be useful when limiting exposure after an IP transfer. | Use as a **limitation‑of‑liability** add‑on to the IP‑assignment clause, especially if the parties wish to cap post‑transfer claims. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_72087_3deb75ce46】 |
| 3 | “Janssen shall indemnify and hold harmless Company, its Affiliates and its and their …” (Clause 12.1.1 – Indemnification) | While not an IP‑assignment clause per se, it provides a **general indemnification** framework that can be tailored to cover IP‑related breaches. | Adapt the indemnity language to create an **IP‑infringement indemnification** provision accompanying the assignment. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_33409_c92ab54a6c】 |
| 4 | “Within thirty (30) days after delivery of such notification, the Indemnifying Party may …” (Clause 12.2.2 – Notice deadline) | Includes a **deadline** and the tag **assignment**, useful for setting a response period for IP‑related notices (e.g., notice of infringement). | Add a **notice‑and‑cure** timeline for IP‑ownership disputes after transfer. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_46790_48db6dbb7a】 |
| 5 | “The Party not controlling such defense shall reasonably cooperate with the other Party.” (Clause 12.2.3 – Cooperation) | Provides a **cooperation** obligation that can be applied to joint defense of IP infringement claims after assignment. | Insert as a **co‑defense cooperation** clause in the IP‑assignment section. | 【6a2aae98df796b0bc54e4526:micro_47668_1a305a53e5】 |

**Next step:** Please review the proposed table. If it looks good, I can create the formal tabular review artifact (e.g., a structured review in ContractSense) for you. Let me know if you’d like any changes or to proceed.

All such products, services, concepts, methods, techniques, and new information will be deemed to be our sole and exclusive property and works made-for- hire for <omitted> us.<omitted>You agree that all other data that you create or collect in connection with the System, and in connection with your operation of the Franchised Business (including customer lists and transaction data), is and will be owned exclusively by us during the term of, and after termination or expiration of, this Agreement.<omitted>You hereby grant to us (and agree to obtain from your affiliates, owners, employees, and/or contractors), a perpetual, non-exclusive, and worldwide right to use any such ideas, concepts, methods, techniques and products in any businesses that we and/or our affiliates, franchisees and designees operate. We will have the right to use those ideas, concepts, methods, techniques, and/or products without making payment to you. You agree not to use or allow any other person or entity to use any such concept, method, technique or product without obtaining our prior written approval.

All right, title and interest in and to the Improved Conformis Background IP and KIB Product IP ("Joint IP") shall be owned jointly by the Parties.<omitted>Each Party to whom ownership is to vest in Joint IP by operation of law or by assignment by its employees or Agents agrees to assign and hereby assigns to the other Party an undivided one-half right, title and interest in and to all Joint IP; and to facilitate such assignment, the Party possessing such ownership agrees (i) to regularly ensure that its employees and consultants timely make any appropriate assignments to it; and (ii) at the other Party's reasonable request, to execute and have its employees and consultants execute, as necessary, all assignments and any other documentation to perfect the undivided one-half right, title and interest in and to the other Party of such Joint IP.<omitted>Subject to the limitations set forth in this Agreement, the Joint IP may be used freely by either Party or its Affiliates and licensed to Third Parties by Conformis and its Affiliates, on the one hand, outside of the Buyer Field or by Stryker and its Affiliates, on the other hand, within the Buyer Field, in each case, without the consent of, or duty to account to or notify, the other Party, but, except with respect to external licenses of the Improved Conformis Background IP by Conformis or its Affiliates to Third Parties, any external Third Party license shall be governed in accordance with the last sentence of Section 4.3(c) of the APA.

Each Party hereby assigns to the other Party a joint equal and undivided interest in and to all Joint Inventions (including Joint Improvements) to effect such joint ownership of such Joint Inventions (including Joint Improvements).<omitted>For those countries where a specific license is required for a joint owner of a Joint Invention or Joint Improvement to practice such Joint Invention or Joint Improvement, in such country, each Party hereby grants to the other Party a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license, transferable and sublicensable, under such Party's right, title and interest in and to such Joint Invention or Joint Improvement to freely exploit such Joint Invention or Joint Improvement in such country, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the licenses granted hereunder.<omitted>As between the Parties, the Parties shall jointly own all Inventions (including Improvements) developed, conceived or reduced to practice jointly by or on behalf of both Bioeq and Licensee (such Inventions, Joint Inventions, and such Improvements, Joint Improvements), and all Intellectual Property Rights and Know-How therein.
